content: 1. Prednisone reduces the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required due to the increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 2. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc through its impact on CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 3. Maraviroc and procarbazine may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 4. Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of prochlorperazine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 5. Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of promethazine and promazine by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but monitoring is advised. 6. Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of propafenone and propranolol by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 7. Quercetin decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 8. Maraviroc and quetiapine may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Close monitoring is necessary. 9. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Maraviroc dosage should be reduced to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid or use alternative drugs if necessary. 10. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 11. Maraviroc and ramipril may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 12. Ranolazine increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting on the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Close monitoring is necessary. 13. Red yeast rice increases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Close monitoring is required. 14. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 15. Rifabutin and rifampin decrease the levels or effects of maraviroc by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 16. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 17. Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of risperidone by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 18. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Maraviroc dosage should be reduced to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Close monitoring is required. 19. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 20. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 21. Maraviroc and sacubitril/valsartan may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting on the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Toxicities should be monitored, and dosage adjustments may be required. 23. Maraviroc and selegiline may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Close monitoring is necessary. 24. Maraviroc increases sertraline levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Close monitoring is required. 25. Maraviroc and sildenafil may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 26. Maraviroc and silodosin may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Close monitoring is necessary. 27. Sirolimus increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting on the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Close monitoring is required. 28. Somatropin decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 29. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting on the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, refer to prescribing information for dosage modifications. 30. Maraviroc and spironolactone may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 31. St. John's Wort decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 32. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting on the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter and altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 33. Tacrolimus increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting on the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Close monitoring is required. 34. Maraviroc and tadalafil may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 35. Maraviroc decreases tamoxifen's effects by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, reducing the formation of its active metabolite, endoxifen. Close monitoring is necessary. 36. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 37. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting as a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness. 38. Maraviroc and telmisartan may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 39. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting on the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended. 40. Maraviroc and terazosin may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 41. Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of thioridazine by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 42. Maraviroc and thiothixene may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Close monitoring is necessary. 43. Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of timolol by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 44. Maraviroc and tizanidine may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Close monitoring is required. 45. Tocilizumab decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 46. Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 47. Tolvaptan increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting on the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Close monitoring is necessary. 48. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 49. Maraviroc and torsemide may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 50. Tovorafenib decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of efficacy. 51. Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of tramadol by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 52. Maraviroc and trandolapril may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 53. Maraviroc and tranylcypromine may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Close monitoring is necessary. 54. Trazodone decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting on the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 55. Maraviroc and treprostinil may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Close monitoring is required. 56. Maraviroc and triamterene may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 57. Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of trifluoperazine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 58. Maraviroc and trimipramine may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Close monitoring is necessary. 59. Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of tropisetron by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 60. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting on the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter and altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose as recommended. 61. Ublituximab decreases the effects of maraviroc through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 62. Maraviroc and valsartan may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 63. Maraviroc and vardenafil may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Close monitoring is required. 64. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Close monitoring is necessary. 65. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Maraviroc dosage should be reduced to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Close monitoring is required. 66. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 67. Maraviroc and ziprasidone may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Close monitoring is necessary. 68. Common adverse effects of maraviroc include upper respiratory infections (20%), musculoskeletal symptoms (15%), cough (13%), fever (12%), rash (11%), dizziness (9%), appetite disorders (8%), herpes infections (8%), bronchitis (7%), sinusitis (7%), constipation (6%), glandular disorders (5%), paresthesia/dysesthesia (5%), renal/urinary disorders (3-5%), depression (4%), disturbed consciousness (4%), peripheral neuropathies (4%), pruritus (4%), sensory abnormalities (4%), folliculitis (3%), hypertension (3%), lipodystrophy (3%), muscle pain (3%), influenza (2%), and pneumonia (2%). 69. Rare but serious adverse effects include cardiac disorders, hepatic cirrhosis, hepatic failure, neoplasms, and central nervous system events. 70. Pregnant women taking maraviroc should be monitored for maternal-fetal outcomes. Patients can be registered by calling 1-800-258-4263. Limited data on pregnancy outcomes are available from the Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry (APR).
